subject.title: fix(exec-approvals): skip socket in YOLO mode regardless of token presence

question: Should node approval-policy writes avoid persisting socket credentials for hosts that do not require an approval socket, while token-bearing gateway and macOS exec-host files retain the strict hardening path?
rationale: The branch trades a real node-exec failure against a bearer-token confidentiality boundary; source and the prior merged design do not establish that a generic `full/off` bypass is safe for every host that may carry persisted socket state.

options.title: Split node token ownership from strict hosts
options.body: Keep the hardened token-bearing store path and change the node-specific write/resolution contract so non-socket node hosts do not persist or rely on a socket credential.

options.title: Accept the YOLO credential bypass
options.body: Allow `full/off` resolution to ignore and leave existing socket credentials unhardened, explicitly accepting the local token-exposure tradeoff.

options.title: Pause this branch
options.body: Leave the PR unmerged until the node-host socket ownership and credential lifecycle have a maintainer-approved design.

recommendation.title: Split node token ownership from strict hosts
recommendation.body: Keep the hardened token-bearing store path and change the node-specific write/resolution contract so non-socket node hosts do not persist or rely on a socket credential.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged no-persistence work established the current strict-versus-no-persistence boundary that this change would alter.
